module_doc:
sink_arg_classifier_ppc64.py: classify exec-class sink argument provenance on PPC64 ELFs.

Gap this fills vs SinkArgClassifier:
  SinkArgClassifier hardcodes x86-64 registers (rdi, rsi, rdx).
  PPC64 ABIv2 passes the first eight arguments in r3-r10.
  That gap is ARCH-GAP-PPC64LE (AdvanceToolchain ppc64le Linux).

Four verdicts (same as all other SinkArgClassifier variants):
  RODATA_CONST     — argument is a constant from .rodata or a literal immediate.
  SNPRINTF_RODATA  — argument is a stack buffer written by snprintf/vsnprintf
                     whose format string is RODATA_CONST.
  ARG_PROPAGATED   — argument traces back to an entry-point r3-r10 register.
  UNKNOWN          — provenance not resolved within the look-back window.

PPC64 ABIv2 calling convention:
  Argument position 0 → r3  (Capstone PPC_REG_R3  = 90)
  Argument position 1 → r4  (Capstone PPC_REG_R4  = 91)
  Argument position 2 → r5  (Capstone PPC_REG_R5  = 92)
  Argument position 3 → r6  (Capstone PPC_REG_R6  = 93)
  Argument position 4 → r7  (Capstone PPC_REG_R7  = 94)
  Argument position 5 → r8  (Capstone PPC_REG_R8  = 95)
  Argument position 6 → r9  (Capstone PPC_REG_R9  = 96)
  Argument position 7 → r10 (Capstone PPC_REG_R10 = 97)
  TOC base → r2 (initialized to .TOC. symbol value at function entry)

PPC64le string address load patterns:
  1. addis rX, r2, HI; addi rX, rX, LO  — TOC-relative addr (most common in ABIv2).
     string_va = toc_base + sign16(HI)<<16 + sign16(LO).
     If string_va in .rodata → RODATA_CONST.
  2. addis rX, r2, HI; ld rX, LO(rX)   — TOC-indirect pointer load.
     ptr_va = toc_base + sign16(HI)<<16 + sign16(LO); val = *ptr_va.
     If val in .rodata → RODATA_CONST.
  3. li rX, imm                          — small immediate (NULL=0, flag).
     RODATA_CONST (literal constant).
  4. mr rX, rY  (or: or rD, rA, rA)     — register copy.  Recurse on rA.
  5. addi rX, r1, N                      — address of stack slot.
     Trigger snprintf backtrack then entry-arg-save detection.
  6. ld rX, N(r1)                        — stack slot load.
     Same backtrack path as addi r1.
  7. ld rX, N(rY)  rY not r1/r2         — struct field / heap offset.
     If rY is an entry-point argument register (r3–r10) → ARG_PROPAGATED.
     Otherwise → UNKNOWN.
  8. Also handles ppc64 BE (EI_DATA=2) via CS_MODE_BIG_ENDIAN.

Note: GOT-relative loads through unknown base registers are UNKNOWN.
Only addis-r2 patterns (absolute TOC-relative) are fully resolved.

Usage:
    from ablation.analyzers.binary_context import BinaryContext
    from ablation.analyzers.sink_arg_classifier_ppc64 import SinkArgClassifierPPC64

    ctx = BinaryContext.load_or_build('/path/to/gcc')
    clf = SinkArgClassifierPPC64.from_context(ctx)
    results = clf.classify_all()
    print(clf.report(results))

module_doc:
sink_arg_classifier_ppc64_elfv1.py: classify exec-class sink argument provenance
on PPC64 BE ELFv1 ELFs (POWER Linux, e.g. IBM LoadLeveler, iAccess, PE bundle).

Gap this fills vs SinkArgClassifier:
  SinkArgClassifier hardcodes x86-64 CALL scanning (E8 opcode) and register names.
  PPC64 BE ELFv1 dispatches via 7-instruction TOC-relative inline stubs; callers
  reach sinks with ``bl <stub_va>`` where stub_va is mapped by BinaryContext's
  _extract_plt_ppc64be().  That stub scan is LOADL-GAP-002.

PPC64 BE ELFv1 ABI calling convention (same registers as PPC32):
  Argument position 0 → r3  (Capstone PPC_REG_R3  = 90)
  Argument position 1 → r4  (Capstone PPC_REG_R4  = 91)
  Argument position 2 → r5  (Capstone PPC_REG_R5  = 92)
  …
  Argument position 7 → r10 (Capstone PPC_REG_R10 = 97)

PPC64 BE string-address load patterns (superset of PPC32):
  1. lis rX, HI; addi rX, rX, LO   — 32-bit signed address (same as PPC32).
  2. lis rX, HI; ori  rX, rX, LO   — 32-bit unsigned address; LO zero-extended.
     string_va = ((HI & 0xFFFF) << 16) | (LO & 0xFFFF).
  3. lis rX, HI; lwz  rX, LO(rX)   — indirect 32-bit pointer (same as PPC32).
  4. lis rX, HI; ld   rX, LO(rX)   — indirect 64-bit pointer.
  5. li  rX, imm                    — small immediate (NULL=0, flag).
  6. mr  rX, rY  (or rD, rA, rA)   — register copy; recurse on rA.
  7. addi rX, r1, N                 — address of stack slot.
  8. ld   rX, N(r1)                 — 64-bit stack slot load.
  9. lwz  rX, N(r1)                 — 32-bit stack slot load (struct with 32-bit fields).
  10. addis rX, r2, HI; addi rX, rX, LO   — TOC-relative address.
      toc_addr = r2 + sign_ext16(HI)<<16 + sign_ext16(LO); RODATA_CONST if in .rodata.
  11. addis rX, r2, HI; ld rX, LO(rX)     — TOC-relative pointer dereference.
      ptr_va = r2 + sign_ext16(HI)<<16 + sign_ext16(LO); RODATA_CONST if *ptr in .rodata.

Usage:
    from ablation.analyzers.binary_context import BinaryContext
    from ablation.analyzers.sink_arg_classifier_ppc64_elfv1 import SinkArgClassifierPPC64ELFv1

    ctx = BinaryContext.load_or_build('/path/to/LoadL_master')
    clf = SinkArgClassifierPPC64ELFv1.from_context(ctx)
    results = clf.classify_all()
    print(clf.report(results))
    flagged = [r for r in results if r.verdict not in ('RODATA_CONST', 'SNPRINTF_RODATA')]

module_doc:
sink_arg_classifier_ppc64_elfv2.py: classify exec-class sink argument provenance
on PPC64 LE ELFv2 ELFs (RHEL/RHCOS ppc64le, HMC management binaries, etc.).

Why this exists
---------------
SinkArgClassifierPPC64ELFv1 handles big-endian ELFv1 (AIX/LoadLeveler TOC stubs).
ppc64le ELFv2 (RHEL-built HMC binaries, IBM PowerSC, RSCT) uses little-endian
encoding and ELFv2 ABIs: standard GOT-indirect PLT stubs and r2 = .got + 0x8000.
The generic SinkArgClassifier falls back to x86_64 Capstone, which produces garbage
on ppc64le code and returns 0 results.  This module closes that gap.

Gap this fills
--------------
All ppc64le (EI_DATA=1) ELFs with exec-class PLT entries returned SAC=0 because
sac_for_context() dispatched to the x86_64 SinkArgClassifier.  HMC management
binaries (hmc.mgmt, hmc.common, hmc.svrmgmt) contain 35+ such binaries.

ELFv2 vs ELFv1 differences handled here
-----------------------------------------
1. Capstone mode: CS_MODE_LITTLE_ENDIAN (EI_DATA=1) vs CS_MODE_BIG_ENDIAN.
2. TOC (r2) discovery: r2 = .got.virtual_address + 0x8000 (GNU ld ELFv2 convention)
   instead of reading from .opd[8].
3. Pointer reads: little-endian (<Q, <I) instead of big-endian (>Q, >I).
4. Rodata ranges: same LIEF section scan, LE binary.

Calling convention (identical to ELFv1 — same Power ABI)
----------------------------------------------------------
  Argument position 0 → r3  (Capstone PPC_REG_R3  = 90)
  Argument position 1 → r4  (PPC_REG_R4  = 91)
  ...
  Argument position 7 → r10 (PPC_REG_R10 = 97)

String-address load patterns (same instructions as ELFv1, LE-encoded)
----------------------------------------------------------------------
  1. lis rX, HI; addi rX, rX, LO         — 32-bit signed address
  2. lis rX, HI; ori  rX, rX, LO         — 32-bit unsigned address
  3. lis rX, HI; lwz  rX, LO(rX)         — indirect 32-bit pointer
  4. lis rX, HI; ld   rX, LO(rX)         — indirect 64-bit pointer
  5. li  rX, imm                          — small immediate / NULL
  6. mr  rX, rY                           — register copy; recurse on rY
  7. addi rX, r1, N                       — address of stack slot
  8. ld   rX, N(r1)                       — 64-bit stack slot load
  9. lwz  rX, N(r1)                       — 32-bit stack slot load
 10. addis rX, r2, HI; addi rX, rX, LO   — TOC-relative address
 11. addis rX, r2, HI; ld rX, LO(rX)     — TOC-relative pointer dereference
 12. ld   rX, N(r2)                       — direct TOC slot dereference
 13. addis rX, r2, HI; [addi rX, rX, LO]; addi r3, rX, OFF — callee-saved base
     register loaded at function entry beyond the 80-instruction backward window.
     (PPC64-SAC-CALLEE-001: full-function forward scan via _eval_callee_saved_reg)

Usage
-----
    from ablation.analyzers.binary_context import BinaryContext
    from ablation.analyzers.sink_arg_classifier_ppc64_elfv2 import SinkArgClassifierPPC64ELFv2

    ctx = BinaryContext.load_or_build('/path/to/hmc_mgmt_binary')
    clf = SinkArgClassifierPPC64ELFv2.from_context(ctx)
    results = clf.classify_all()
    print(clf.report(results))
    flagged = [r for r in results if r.verdict not in ('RODATA_CONST', 'SNPRINTF_RODATA')]

classes.name: SinkArgClassifierPPC64ELFv2
classes.doc:
Classify exec-class sink call-site argument provenance on PPC64 LE ELFv2 ELFs.

Fills the ppc64le analysis gap: sac_for_context() previously dispatched to the
x86_64 SinkArgClassifier for EI_DATA=1 ppc64 binaries, returning 0 results.

methods.name: _remap_plt_rev_to_stubs
methods.doc:
Scan non-.text executable sections for ppc64le ELFv2 PLT call stubs
and remap _plt_rev entries from GOT VAs to the callable stub VAs.

methods.name: _eval_callee_saved_reg
methods.doc:
Forward-pass constant propagation for a callee-saved register.

PPC64 ELFv2 callee-saved registers (r14-r31) are often loaded once at
function entry with a TOC-relative address and then used as base registers
throughout the function — far beyond the 80-instruction backward window.
This scan tracks the deterministic value of reg_id from function start up
to use_idx by following:
  addis rX, r2, HI          -> rX = r2 + sign16(HI)<<16
  addi  rX, rX, LO          -> rX += sign16(LO)  (only when base == rX)
  ld    rX, N(r2)           -> rX = mem[r2 + sign16(N)]  (direct GOT load)
Any other write invalidates the known value (returns None).

methods.name: _is_callee_saved_from_entry_arg
methods.doc:
Return True if the most recent write to reg_id before use_idx was
'mr reg_id, rY' where rY is an entry-arg register (r3-r10).

Handles 'ld r3, N(r26)' where r26 = mr r26, r3 (entry arg struct ptr).
The backward scan is the same direction as _trace_arg to get the effective
value at the call site (not the function-entry value).
(PPC64-SAC-CALLEE-001)

methods.name: _scan_uncovered_bls
methods.doc:
Fallback: scan .text bytes directly for BL <stub_va> when func_starts
misses the containing function (e.g. ppc64le ELFv2 large Go DSOs where
BinaryContext doesn't register every GEP as a func_start).

For each uncovered BL hit, disassemble a 256-instruction window ending
at the call site and classify as if called from a pseudo func_start.

methods.name: classify_all
methods.doc: Run classification across all func_starts for all registered sink call sites.

methods.name: classify_sink
methods.doc: Run classification for a single named sink only.

module_doc:
sink_arg_classifier_s390.py: classify exec-class sink argument provenance on
s390 (31-bit) and s390x (64-bit) BE ELFs.

Gap this fills (S390-GAP-001):
  BinaryContext detects ELF e_machine 0x0016 (EM_S390) and falls through to its
  x86_64 PLT parser, which returns plt=0 (parse failure) — masking any exec-class
  dynamic imports.  Ablation SinkArgClassifier therefore cannot run.  This module
  uses LIEF directly for DYNSYM enumeration and Capstone CS_ARCH_SYSZ for
  disassembly, completely bypassing BinaryContext's broken s390x path.

Evidence for this gap: IBM ClearCase linux_390 (cleartool, 20516 bytes), IBM
Rational BuildForge 7.1.1.3 bfagent (s390x), IBM XL C/C++ Compiler 1.2.0 for
s390x — all returned BinaryContext.arch='x86_64' with plt=0.

Four verdicts (consistent with all other SinkArgClassifier variants):
  RODATA_CONST     — argument is a .rodata address or literal immediate.
  SNPRINTF_RODATA  — stack buffer filled by snprintf with a .rodata format string.
  ARG_PROPAGATED   — argument traces back to an entry-point register (r2–r6).
  UNKNOWN          — provenance not resolved within the look-back window.

s390x System V ABI (both 31-bit s390 and 64-bit s390x):
  Argument 0 → r2    Argument 1 → r3    Argument 2 → r4
  Argument 3 → r5    Argument 4 → r6

s390x string-address load patterns handled:
  1. larl  %rX, addr        PC-relative address load.
                            If addr in .rodata → RODATA_CONST.
  2. lghi  %rX, imm         16-bit sign-extended immediate → RODATA_CONST (NULL/literal).
     lhi   %rX, imm
  3. lgfi  %rX, imm         32-bit sign-extended immediate → RODATA_CONST.
  4. lgr   %rX, %rY  /      Register copy.  Recurse on source register.
     lr    %rX, %rY
  5. la    %rX, N(%r15)     Address of stack slot; trigger snprintf back-track.
     lay   %rX, N(%r15)
  6. lgrl  %rX, addr        64-bit load from PC-relative address.
                            If target in .rodata → RODATA_CONST.
  7. lg    %rX, N(%rY)      64-bit load from memory.
     l     %rX, N(%rY)      If rY is an entry-arg register (r2–r6) → ARG_PROPAGATED.

Usage:
    from ablation.analyzers.binary_context import BinaryContext
    from ablation.analyzers.sink_arg_classifier_s390 import SinkArgClassifierS390X

    ctx = BinaryContext.load_or_build('/path/to/bfagent')
    clf = SinkArgClassifierS390X.from_path(ctx.path)  # bypass BinaryContext PLT gap

    results = clf.classify_all()
    print(clf.report(results))

classes.name: SinkArgClassifierS390X
classes.doc:
Classify exec-class sink call-site argument provenance on s390/s390x BE ELFs.

Fills S390-GAP-001: BinaryContext returns plt=0 for s390/s390x (e_machine=0x0016)
due to architecture detection mismatch.  Use from_path() instead of from_context()
to bypass BinaryContext's broken s390 PLT path.

methods.name: from_path
methods.doc: Construct directly from file path, bypassing BinaryContext's s390 gap.

methods.name: from_context
methods.doc: Accept a BinaryContext for API consistency; uses ctx.path internally.

methods.name: add_sink
methods.doc: Register a vendor-specific exec-class sink.

methods.name: _get_plt_va
methods.doc:
Return the PLT stub VA for sym_name, or None.
s390x PLT layout: stub[0]=resolver (32 bytes), stub[N]=plt_base+32*(N+1).
R_390_JMP_SLOT relocations in .rela.plt are ordered; their 0-indexed rank
gives stub N.

methods.name: _classify_reg
methods.doc: Walk backwards from call_idx to determine argument register provenance.

methods.name: _check_snprintf_fill
methods.doc:
Return SNPRINTF_RODATA if the stack slot was filled by snprintf with a
.rodata format string within _SNPRINTF_WINDOW instructions before the call.

methods.name: _raw_brasl_scan
methods.doc:
Byte-sweep a raw code segment for BRASL instructions whose target is a
PLT sink.  Used for stripped binaries where ELF FUNC symbols do not cover
the actual code.

s390x BRASL encoding: 0xC0 0xE5 <i32 half-word offset> (6 bytes).
target = call_va + 2 * sign_extend_32(offset)
We verify each hit with Capstone before running the argument trace.

methods.name: classify_all
methods.doc:
Find all exec-class sink call sites in this binary and classify each.
Returns a list of SinkClassification named tuples.

For non-stripped binaries the ELF FUNC symbols cover all functions.
For stripped binaries (no .symtab) the symbol set covers only exported
entries (typically OpenSSL/libc glue) and misses the actual application
code.  In that case a raw BRASL byte-sweep over the .text section is used
to locate call sites, bypassing the need for function-boundary symbols.

methods.name: is_s390
methods.doc: Return True if the file is an s390 or s390x ELF (e_machine == 0x0016).

module_doc:
sink_arg_classifier_x86_32.py: classify exec-class sink argument provenance on x86_32 ELFs.

Gap this fills vs SinkArgClassifier:
  SinkArgClassifier hardcodes x86-64 registers (rdi, rsi, rdx).
  x86_32 cdecl passes all arguments on the stack (pushed right-to-left).
  That gap is RMC-GAP-002 / COMMSVR-GAP-004 / HACMP-GAP-001.
  This module resolves all three.

Session 20 improvements (2026-10-19):
  [A] [reg+disp] dereference → ARG_PROPAGATED when base register traces to ARG_PROPAGATED.
      Fixes execv(argv[0], argv) pattern where arg0 = [eax] and eax = [ebp+8].
      Prior: UNKNOWN. Now: ARG_PROPAGATED.
  [B] strcpy/strcat-family added to _backtrack_stack_slot.
      Fixes strcpy(buf, RODATA); system(buf) — buffer filled from static string.
      Prior: UNKNOWN. Now: SNPRINTF_RODATA.
  Gap IDs: SYNERGY-UNKNOWN-001 (execv argv deref), SYNERGY-UNKNOWN-002 (strcpy fill).

Session 49 fix (2026-10-22): X86-32-SNPRINTF-GAP-001
  SNPRINTF_RODATA was returned for sprintf(buf, "cmd %s", net_input) → system(buf)
  because only the format string position was checked, not the format string content
  or its variadic arguments.  Demonstrated by DOORS-002: system() at 0x8076373 was
  classified SNPRINTF_RODATA when the format string "unzip … '%s'" has a %s arg that
  comes from a DBP network packet.
  Fix: _backtrack_stack_slot now reads the format string bytes via _try_get_imm_va +
  _read_cstr, counts non-%% specifiers, and calls _snprintf_variadic_verdict to
  classify each variadic argument.  No specifiers → SNPRINTF_RODATA unchanged.
  Any ARG_PROPAGATED variadic arg → ARG_PROPAGATED.  Any UNKNOWN → UNKNOWN.
  Gap ID: X86-32-SNPRINTF-GAP-001.

Four verdicts (same as SinkArgClassifier):
  RODATA_CONST     — argument is a constant from .rodata or a literal immediate.
  SNPRINTF_RODATA  — argument is a stack buffer written by snprintf/sprintf
                     whose format string is RODATA_CONST.
  ARG_PROPAGATED   — argument traces back to [ebp + N] (N > 0): a function argument.
  UNKNOWN          — provenance not resolved within the look-back window.

x86_32 cdecl calling convention:
  Args are pushed right-to-left. The LAST push before call = arg_pos 0 (first arg).
  Argument position 0 → last push  (closest to call instruction)
  Argument position 1 → second-to-last push
  Argument position 2 → third-to-last push
  ...

x86_32 string address patterns:
  1. push imm                              — direct pointer; check if imm in .rodata.
  2. lea eax, [ebx - N] / lea eax, [ebx+N]— GOT-relative: ebx = GOT base (PIC via
                                             call/pop + add ebx, N); -N/+N is .rodata offset.
                                             Then push eax.
  3. mov eax, [ebp + N] (N > 0)           — function argument → ARG_PROPAGATED.
  4. mov eax, [ebp - N]                   — stack local; check snprintf backtrack.
  5. lea eax, [ebp - N]                   — address of stack local; snprintf backtrack.
  6. push reg                              — trace register backward to its origin.
  7. sub esp, N then mov [esp+M], val     — slot-style arg passing; trace val.

Usage:
    from ablation.analyzers.binary_context import BinaryContext
    from ablation.analyzers.sink_arg_classifier_x86_32 import SinkArgClassifierI386

    ctx = BinaryContext.load_or_build('/path/to/rmcd', force_rebuild=True)
    clf = SinkArgClassifierI386.from_context(ctx)

    # Add strcpy as a sink to classify BOF candidates (arg_pos=1 = source string)
    clf.add_sink('strcpy',  arg_pos=1)
    clf.add_sink('sprintf', arg_pos=1)   # fmt string is arg_pos=1

    results = clf.classify_all()
    print(clf.report(results))

    # Filter to non-safe findings only
    flagged = [r for r in results if r.verdict not in ('RODATA_CONST',)]

classes.name: SinkArgClassifierI386
classes.doc:
Classify exec-class sink call site argument provenance on x86_32 ELFs.

Handles the cdecl calling convention: args pushed right-to-left, so the
LAST push before the call instruction is arg_pos=0 (the first argument).

This module fills RMC-GAP-002, COMMSVR-GAP-004, and HACMP-GAP-001.

methods.name: from_context
methods.doc: Build from a BinaryContext.

methods.name: from_path
methods.doc: Build directly from an ELF path — constructs BinaryContext internally.

methods.name: add_sink
methods.doc: Register an additional sink (e.g., 'strcpy' at arg_pos=1 for source).

methods.name: _read_cstr
methods.doc: Return null-terminated printable ASCII at va, or None if not a string.

methods.name: _is_static_const
methods.doc: True if va holds a compile-time string constant (.rodata or .data init).

methods.name: _find_sink_plts
methods.doc:
Return {sink_va: (name, arg_pos)} for sinks present in the PLT.

Do NOT gate on callers_of(): BinaryContext's call graph is x86_64-only
and returns [] for i386 binaries, which would mark every import as dead.
classify_all() scans all func_starts instead.

methods.name: _find_call_sites
methods.doc: Return indices of call instructions that target sink_va.

methods.name: _classify_value
methods.doc:
Classify a value's provenance by scanning backward from start_idx.

target forms:
  'imm:<N>'       — immediate value (check .rodata membership)
  'reg:<id>'      — register to trace backward
  'stack:<N>'     — stack slot [ebp-N] to trace backward (local var)
  'arg:<N>'       — [ebp+N] (N > 0) — already classified as ARG_PROPAGATED

methods.name: _writes_reg
methods.doc:
True if the instruction's first operand is a register destination (writes reg_id).

Excludes instructions where the first operand is a source: push, cmp, test,
jmp, call.  Without this exclusion, 'push esi' would be mistaken for a write
to ESI, causing _classify_value() to stop at the push rather than continuing
backward to the lea that actually loads ESI.

methods.name: _classify_lea
methods.doc:
Classify a lea instruction.
lea eax, [abs_addr]   → direct absolute address; check if in .rodata
lea eax, [ebx + N]    → GOT-relative; check if target is .rodata
lea eax, [ebp - N]    → address of stack local; snprintf backtrack
lea eax, [ebp + N]    → address of function arg (rare); ARG_PROPAGATED

methods.name: _classify_mov
methods.doc: Classify a mov instruction that writes to dest_reg.

methods.name: _find_ebx_got_base
methods.doc:
Find the GOT base value in ebx.

Two PIC x86_32 patterns:
  1. call $+5 / pop ebx / add ebx, DELTA  — used in hand-written or old GCC code.
     pop_va = address of pop ebx; got_base = pop_va + DELTA.

  2. call __x86_get_pc_thunk_bx / add ebx, DELTA  — GCC PIC standard.
     Thunk body: mov ebx, [esp]; ret — so on return, ebx = return address
     = address of the instruction after the call = address of the add itself.
     got_base = add_insn.address + DELTA.

methods.name: _find_pop_ebx_va
methods.doc: Find the VA of the 'pop ebx' that precedes the 'add ebx, N'.

methods.name: _has_pc_thunk_call
methods.doc:
Return True if a call to __x86_get_pc_thunk_bx (or equivalent) immediately
precedes the 'add ebx, N' at add_idx.

Two identification strategies:
  - Named: call target matches a known PLT/export entry with 'get_pc_thunk'
    or 'i686.get_pc.thunk' in its name.
  - Structural: any call within 4 instructions before the add where the
    callee is a tiny (≤8 byte) function — GCC always emits the thunk as
    a tiny helper near the call site.

methods.name: _try_get_imm_va
methods.doc:
Return the VA of the argument if it is a direct push-immediate RODATA pointer.
Returns None for GOT-relative or register-based patterns.

methods.name: _snprintf_variadic_verdict
methods.doc:
Check variadic arguments to snprintf/sprintf after confirming the format
string is RODATA_CONST.  Close X86-32-SNPRINTF-GAP-001: a format string
that contains %s/%d/… with user-controlled arguments was previously
returned as SNPRINTF_RODATA (false-safe), hiding vulnerabilities like
sprintf(buf, "unzip -o '%s'", network_path) → system(buf).

Algorithm:
  1. Read the format string.  If unreadable → conservative UNKNOWN.
  2. Count non-%% % specifiers.  If none → the buffer is truly static → SNPRINTF_RODATA.
  3. For each variadic position, call _get_pushed_arg.
     ARG_PROPAGATED dominates; accumulate UNKNOWN as fallback.

methods.name: _backtrack_stack_slot
methods.doc:
Determine if a stack slot [ebp - ebp_neg_offset] was filled by a string-building
call (snprintf/sprintf or strcpy/strcat) with a RODATA source.
Returns SNPRINTF_RODATA, ARG_PROPAGATED, or UNKNOWN.

methods.name: _arg_is_stack_slot
methods.doc: Check if the arg at arg_pos to the call at call_idx is lea eax, [ebp - ebp_neg_offset].

methods.name: _find_push_for_arg
methods.doc:
Find the instruction index that provides argument arg_pos.

Handles two x86_32 cdecl calling convention styles:
  Push-based (O0): push <val> instructions right-to-left.
    arg_pos 0 = last push, arg_pos 1 = second-to-last, etc.
  Sub-esp+mov (O1+): frame pre-allocated by sub esp,N; args written
    as mov dword ptr [esp + N*4], val.
    arg_pos N → look for mov [esp + N*4], val.

methods.name: _get_pushed_arg
methods.doc:
Get the classification verdict for arg_pos at the call at call_idx.
Returns verdict string or None if the argument couldn't be found.

Handles both push-based and sub-esp+mov calling styles.
For push: ops[0] is the value.
For mov [esp+N], val: ops[0] is the destination, ops[1] is the value.

methods.name: classify_all
methods.doc:
Classify argument provenance for all call sites of all registered sinks.
Returns a list of SinkClassification objects.

methods.name: report
methods.doc: Format results as a human-readable report.

module_doc:
sink_propagator.py — Transitive sink-wrapper discovery for x86-64 ELF binaries.

4 things that weren't possible before in Ablation:

1. **Find injection paths hidden behind custom string-passing wrappers.**
   TaintTracker searches for calls to known PLT sinks (system, popen, etc.).
   When a binary wraps system() behind doSystem(string) and systemLog(char*)
   — three levels deep — TaintTracker finds zero injection sites while the
   vulnerability is fully reachable. SinkPropagator computes the transitive
   closure of passthrough wrappers so TaintTracker gets the complete sink list.

2. **Detect the entire wrapper chain, not just level-one wrappers.**
   Propagation iterates to a fixed point: if addUser() passes its arg to
   doSystem(), and doSystem() passes its arg to systemLog(), and systemLog()
   calls system() — all three are returned as SinkWrapper findings with their
   full lineage. A single TaintTracker run using the expanded sink list will
   then trace injection all the way from the entry point.

3. **Report multi-parameter wrappers.** Some wrappers pass argument 1 (rsi)
   rather than argument 0 (rdi) — e.g., openlog(ident, opts, facility) where
   ident at rdi becomes the format string for an internal vfprintf. The scanner
   tracks which parameter index is propagated and emits the correct arg_pos for
   each wrapper, so TaintTracker traces the right source register.

4. **Give a human-readable chain report.** Each SinkWrapper record carries the
   full ancestor chain (which sink it wraps, and what that sink wraps, etc.)
   so a reviewer can follow the injection path without re-running capstone by
   hand.

Usage::

    from ablation.analyzers.sink_propagator import SinkPropagator

    sp = SinkPropagator.from_path('/path/to/binary')
    wrappers = sp.propagate()
    print(sp.report(wrappers))

    # Use expanded sinks with TaintTracker:
    from ablation.analyzers.taint_tracker_x86 import TaintTrackerX86
    tt = TaintTrackerX86.from_path('/path/to/binary')
    for w in wrappers:
        tt.add_sink(w.va, arg_pos=w.param_idx)
    results = tt.run()

Arch guard: raises ValueError for non-x86-64 ELF.

classes.name: SinkWrapper
classes.doc: A function that passes one of its arguments through to a known sink.

classes.name: SinkPropagator
classes.doc:
Discover passthrough wrappers around dangerous sinks in an x86-64 ELF.

Starting from known PLT sinks, iterates to a fixed point: any function
that passes its parameter through to a (PLT or previously discovered)
sink is itself a sink, and its callers are checked in the next round.

methods.name: add_sink
methods.doc: Add a vendor-specific sink by PLT name.

methods.name: propagate
methods.doc:
Compute transitive closure of sink wrappers.

Returns a list of SinkWrapper objects, one per discovered wrapper
function, in discovery order (level-1 first, then deeper levels).

methods.name: _find_prologue_spills
methods.doc:
Scan function prologue for `mov [rbp - N], <arg_reg>`.
Returns {-N: arg_idx} where arg_idx is 0-based param position.
Only scans the first 20 instructions (pre-spill area).

methods.name: _trace_rdi_at
methods.doc:
Backwards-trace from call_idx to find which parameter index rdi holds
at that call. Returns the parameter index (0-based) or None.

Handles 1-hop via rax: mov rdi, [rbp-N] or mov rax, [rbp-N]; mov rdi, rax.

methods.name: _insn_sets_reg
methods.doc: Return True if insn's first operand is reg_id (i.e., the insn sets reg_id).

methods.name: _reg_canonical
methods.doc: Map 32-bit / 16-bit / 8-bit aliases back to the 64-bit register ID.

methods.name: _check_wrapper
methods.doc:
Disassemble func_va. If it contains exactly one call to a known sink
AND that call receives an argument that traces back to the function's
own parameter, return a SinkWrapper. Otherwise return None.

We require exactly one sink call per function to avoid false positives
from dispatch functions that conditionally call different sinks.

module_doc:
sink_sanitizer_filter.py: post-process ARG_PROPAGATED SinkArgClassifier results
to detect sanitizer-gated exec sinks and reclassify them as SANITIZER_VALIDATED.

The biggest manual bottleneck in a sink-triage engagement is distinguishing
ARG_PROPAGATED sites that are structurally safe (the argument passes through a
shell-safe allowlist validator before reaching the exec sink) from those that are
genuinely exploitable.  Every ARG_PROPAGATED site must otherwise be manually
disassembled and traced — a 30–60 minute task per site on a stripped binary.

SinkArgClassifier identifies where exec-sink arguments originate.
SanitizerDetector identifies which functions enforce a shell-safe character
allowlist.  This module connects the two: for each ARG_PROPAGATED site it
disassembles the containing function and verifies three conditions:

  1. A SHELL_SAFE sanitizer is called on the same argument somewhere before
     the exec sink within the same basic region (up to _SANITIZER_SCAN_WINDOW
     instructions back).
  2. A conditional branch on the sanitizer's return value guards execution:
     test eax, eax / jz <error> means execution does not reach the exec sink
     when the sanitizer rejects.
  3. The argument register at the sanitizer call traces to the same source
     register as the argument at the exec call (same variable, not a
     different string that happens to share register rdi momentarily).

Sites meeting all three conditions are reclassified SANITIZER_VALIDATED
(severity lowered from HIGH to LOW).  Sites that partially match are left
ARG_PROPAGATED with detail unchanged.

Confirmed engagement gap (TG-FAD-2): on FortiADC authd, auth_sso_krb
(0xd930) was manually confirmed as the only ARG_PROPAGATED site without
a sanitizer guard.  Five other ARG_PROPAGATED sites in the same binary
would have been automatically downgraded had this module existed.

Usage:
    from ablation.analyzers.sink_sanitizer_filter import SinkSanitizerFilter
    from ablation.analyzers.sink_arg_classifier import SinkArgClassifier

    clf = SinkArgClassifier.from_path('/path/to/binary')
    results = clf.classify_all()

    flt = SinkSanitizerFilter.from_path('/path/to/binary')
    results = flt.apply(results)

    # Only exploit candidates (not sanitizer-gated)
    hot = [r for r in results
           if r.verdict not in ('RODATA_CONST', 'SNPRINTF_RODATA', 'SANITIZER_VALIDATED')]
    print(flt.report(results))

classes.name: SinkSanitizerFilter
classes.doc:
Post-processor for SinkArgClassifier output.

Reclassifies ARG_PROPAGATED sites to SANITIZER_VALIDATED where the argument
demonstrably passes through a SHELL_SAFE allowlist validator before the exec
sink, and a conditional branch on the validator's return value gates execution.

methods.name: _va_to_bytes
methods.doc: Return `length` raw bytes starting at virtual address `va`, or None.

methods.name: _disasm_func
methods.doc: Disassemble the function at func_va, up to 4096 bytes or next function start.

methods.name: _find_sanitizer_and_guard
methods.doc:
Scan backward from exec_idx for a SHELL_SAFE sanitizer call that is
subsequently guarded by a conditional branch on eax.

Returns (sanitizer_call_idx, guard_branch_idx, sanitizer_name) or None.
The guard must appear within _GUARD_SCAN_WINDOW instructions after the
sanitizer call and must test eax/al/rax before a conditional jump.

methods.name: _try_upgrade
methods.doc:
Try to upgrade clf from ARG_PROPAGATED to SANITIZER_VALIDATED.

Returns a new SinkClassification on success, None on failure.
Arg-identity check: rdi at sanitizer call and rdi at exec call must trace
to the same source register (same variable, not a coincidentally shared rdi).

methods.name: apply
methods.doc:
Post-process SinkArgClassifier output.

Returns a new list; ARG_PROPAGATED entries are upgraded to
SANITIZER_VALIDATED where all three conditions are confirmed.
All other entries (RODATA_CONST, SNPRINTF_RODATA, UNKNOWN) are unchanged.

methods.name: report
methods.doc: Format a triage summary after apply().

functions.name: _reg_canon
functions.doc: Return canonical 64-bit register name, or the input lower-cased if unknown.

functions.name: _trace_first_arg_source
functions.doc:
Trace rdi at insns[call_idx] backward to find its ultimate source register.

Returns:
  - Canonical register name (e.g. 'r14', 'rdi') — the register that last
    wrote to rdi before this call.
  - 'STACK' if rdi was set via lea [rsp/rbp + N] (stack buffer address).
  - None if the source cannot be determined within _TRACE_LOOKBACK instructions
    (ambiguous memory dereference, xor, or clobber by a call).

One level of non-volatile register follow: if `mov rdi, r14` is found, the
function continues backward looking for what set r14.  Only non-volatile
registers are followed (r12–r15, rbx, rbp) — caller-saved regs (rsi, rdx, …)
are not followed because a call between the setter and the use would clobber
them, breaking the chain.

Stops at a CALL instruction when the current target register is caller-saved,
since the callee may return a new value via rax that gets moved into the target.

functions.name: _call_target_from_ops
functions.doc: Return direct call target VA from capstone op_str, or None for indirect.

module_doc:
source_arch_risk.py: "safe now catastrophic later" architectural risk scanner.

Detects files that combine unsafe rendering primitives with extensible type
dispatchers, string-based component selectors, or shared-module context.

The risk model: a file is low-risk if it only has one tag category. It becomes
high-risk when unsafe rendering lives in the same file as a type-dispatch switch
or string-based selector, because those are the exact patterns developers extend
by adding new cases — without realising each new case is a new rendering path
that may bypass shared sanitization.

Tag categories:
    unsafe_render  — StrictUnsafe, unsafeHTML, innerHTML, eval, dangerouslySetInnerHTML
    type_dispatch  — switch/if on *Type, *Action, *Policy, *Component, *Kind
    string_selector — hardcoded element-name string property, template-literal tag name
    registry_lookup — customElements.get(), componentRegistry[], createElement(variable)
    shared_module  — file in elements/, common/, admin/policies/; class extends Base*/ViewSet

Risk score = count of distinct categories present. HIGH_CONFIDENCE when a known
dangerous combo appears (unsafe_render + type_dispatch, unsafe_render + string_selector, etc.)

Usage:
    from ablation.analyzers.source_ingestion import SourceContext
    from ablation.analyzers.source_arch_risk import SourceArchRiskScanner

    ctx = SourceContext.from_path("/tmp/authentik")
    scanner = SourceArchRiskScanner.from_context(ctx)
    findings = scanner.scan()
    print(scanner.report(findings, min_score=2))

    # Only unsafe_render findings in shared modules
    high = [f for f in findings if f.score >= 3 or f.high_confidence]

CLI:
    python3 -m ablation.analyzers.source_arch_risk /tmp/authentik
    python3 -m ablation.analyzers.source_arch_risk /tmp/authentik --min-score 2
    python3 -m ablation.analyzers.source_arch_risk /tmp/authentik --tag unsafe_render
    python3 -m ablation.analyzers.source_arch_risk /tmp/authentik --ext ts py

module_doc:
source_audit_compressor.py — Source Code Auditor.

Audit any large codebase for security vulnerabilities. Every source file gets a
5-bit security profile that determines exactly how much attention it needs, so
nothing gets missed and nothing gets read twice.

The core insight: most source files share identical security-relevant profiles.
Files with the same profile are auditable as a batch — read one representative,
apply the finding to all others in the same profile bucket.

Profile = 5-bit integer (0–31) encoding the presence of security-relevant signals:

    bit 4 (weight 16): has_unsafe_render  — unsafeHTML / innerHTML / StrictUnsafe / eval
    bit 3 (weight  8): has_href_binding   — dynamic href=${...} attribute
    bit 2 (weight  4): has_url_assignment — window.location.assign / window.open(var)
    bit 1 (weight  2): has_user_data      — renders .name/.username/.body/.email/.description
    bit 0 (weight  1): is_shared_module   — elements/, common/, admin/policies/, Base* class

Profile 0 (00000): No sinks, no hrefs, no URL assignments, no user data, leaf component.
  → Batch-CLEAN after one representative read. This is the vast majority of files.

Profile 16+ (1xxxx): Has unsafe rendering.
  → Individual read required for every file.

Profile 8–15 (01xxx): Has href binding without unsafe rendering.
  → Individual read required (AUT-CHANGELOG-URL-1 class).

Profile 4–7 (001xx): Has URL assignment.
  → Spot-check (usually server-generated URLs, but verify).

Profiles 2–3 (0001x): Has user-data rendering only.
  → Spot-check (text-node context is usually safe, but verify).

Profile 1 (00001): Shared module only, no rendering signals.
  → Batch with other shared-only files after one read.

Compression ratio for a 2861-file TypeScript codebase (empirical):
  ~2790 files in profile 0 → batch on 1 representative read
  ~71 files in profiles 1–31 → individual or spot-check reads
  Audit compression: 2861 reads → ~72 reads (40x reduction)

Usage:
    from ablation.analyzers.source_ingestion import SourceContext
    from ablation.analyzers.source_audit_compressor import SourceAuditCompressor

    ctx = SourceContext.from_path("/tmp/authentik")
    compressor = SourceAuditCompressor.from_context(ctx)
    buckets = compressor.compress()
    print(compressor.report(buckets))

    # Get the individual-read required files (profiles with any unsafe sink)
    priority = compressor.priority_reads(buckets)
    for profile, files in priority:
        print(f"profile={profile:05b} ({len(files)} files) — read all individually")

    # Get the batch-CLEAN candidates (profile 0)
    batch = compressor.batch_clean(buckets)
    print(f"Batch-CLEAN: {len(batch)} files (read 1 representative)")

CLI:
    python3 -m ablation.analyzers.source_audit_compressor /tmp/authentik
    python3 -m ablation.analyzers.source_audit_compressor /tmp/authentik --profile 8
    python3 -m ablation.analyzers.source_audit_compressor /tmp/authentik --ext ts --show-files

source_isolation_checker.py: tenant isolation checker for source RE.

Finds database queries (Prisma, Mongoose, SQLAlchemy, raw SQL) that fetch or
mutate data without scoping to the authenticated tenant (org/project/user).
This is the highest-yield pattern class in multi-tenant SaaS: a missing
projectId / orgId in a where clause → IDOR or cross-tenant data leak.

Pattern: findUnique / findFirst / findMany with no tenant-scoping field in the
where clause. Also detects update/delete/upsert without tenant scope.

Analogous to the interproc_field_writer.py scanner in binary RE (which checks
that tainted fields are written with appropriate bounds), but operating on ORM
call AST patterns instead of instruction sequences.

source_sink_scanner.py: dangerous sink detection for source RE.

Finds dangerous code patterns across a repository: code eval, subprocess
execution, SSRF, path traversal, and unguarded internal endpoints. Each sink
class maps to a CWE and severity. A guard-condition detector narrows findings
by identifying env-var or conditional gates around sinks (reducing HIGH → MEDIUM
for gated sinks, as in LFG-CODEEVAL-1 where vm.runInContext was gated by
LANGFUSE_CODE_EVAL_DISPATCHER=insecure-local).

    scanner = SourceSinkScanner.from_context(ctx)
    findings = scanner.scan()
    print(scanner.report(findings))

    # Filter by severity
    highs = [f for f in findings if f.severity == "HIGH"]

module_doc:
source_taint_tracker.py: inter-procedural taint path tracer for source RE.

Implements backward slicing from dangerous sinks to HTTP route handlers (trust
boundaries). For each sink identified by SourceSinkScanner, walks the call graph
backward until a route handler is reached or the graph is exhausted. Each
confirmed path is a TaintPath: a chain of (file, line, function) hops from
the route handler down to the sink.

Analogous to TaintTracker (x86/ARM/MIPS) in binary RE: same backward-slice
from sink model, same CONFIRMED/PLAUSIBLE verdict system. Operates on regex-
extracted call graphs instead of disassembled instruction operands.

Architecture: lazy grep-per-function
  build()           — scans all TS/JS files for function definition locations
                      (name + line number). Fast and low-memory: no call sites stored.
  _get_callers(fn)  — called during BFS; greps repo for files containing fn(),
                      then parses only those files for the containing function.
                      Results cached — each unique function name is grepped once.

  This means we grep for ~20-50 unique function names (the functions actually
  on the backward path for 3 sinks at depth 6), not all functions in 5237 files.
  Contrast with an eager full call graph which OOMs at 5k+ TS files.

Trust boundary: any file under pages/api/ or app/api/ that exports a default
handler function. These files receive HTTP requests (req.body, req.query, etc.)
and are the source of all user-controlled data in Next.js applications.

Confidence levels:
  DIRECT  : sink is inside a route handler (0 hops)
  HIGH    : route handler → 1 intermediate → sink
  MEDIUM  : route handler → 2 intermediates → sink
  LOW     : route handler → 3+ intermediates → sink (some regex FP risk)

Usage:
    from ablation.analyzers.source_ingestion import SourceContext
    from ablation.analyzers.source_sink_scanner import SourceSinkScanner, SinkHit
    from ablation.analyzers.source_taint_tracker import SourceTaintTracker

    ctx = SourceContext.from_path("/tmp/langfuse")
    tracker = SourceTaintTracker.from_context(ctx)
    tracker.build()

    scanner = SourceSinkScanner.from_context(ctx)
    sinks = [h for h in scanner.scan() if h.severity in ("CRITICAL", "HIGH")]
    paths = tracker.trace_all(sinks)
    print(tracker.report(paths))

CLI:
    python3 -m ablation.analyzers.source_taint_tracker /tmp/langfuse
    python3 -m ablation.analyzers.source_taint_tracker /tmp/langfuse --severity HIGH

module_doc:
sql_sink_scanner.py: detect raw SQL injection in C/C++ ELF binaries that call the
MySQL C API or SQLite3 directly, without a prepared-statement layer.

Classic pattern caught by this scanner:

    snprintf(buf, sizeof(buf), "SELECT ... WHERE login='%s'", username);
    mysql_query(conn, buf);   // SQL injection if username is user-controlled

FormatStringScanner misses this because snprintf is safe by itself.
SqlSinkScanner specifically chains: find SQL sink → trace SQL arg → find format
string builder → inspect format string for %s injection specifiers.

Verdicts:
  INJECTABLE          — format string has %s; argument is not RODATA; high-confidence
  INJECTABLE_LITERAL  — SQL literal in RODATA already contains %s
  RODATA_CONST        — SQL string is a RODATA literal with no %s; safe
  SAFE_NUMERIC        — format string has only %d/%u/%x/etc; no string interpolation
  ARG_PROPAGATED      — SQL string came from an entry-argument register; caller controls it
  UNKNOWN             — provenance not resolved within look-back window

Covered sinks:
  mysql_query(conn, sql)              → RSI (arg1)
  mysql_real_query(conn, sql, len)    → RSI (arg1)
  sqlite3_exec(db, sql, ...)          → RSI (arg1)
  sqlite3_prepare_v2(db, sql, ...)    → RSI (arg1)
  sqlite3_prepare(db, sql, ...)       → RSI (arg1)

Usage:
    from ablation.analyzers.sql_sink_scanner import SqlSinkScanner

    scanner = SqlSinkScanner.from_path('/path/to/binary')
    findings = scanner.scan()
    print(scanner.report(findings))

    # Filter to injection candidates only
    injections = [f for f in findings if f.verdict == SqlSinkScanner.INJECTABLE]

CLI:
    python3 -m ablation.analyzers.sql_sink_scanner /path/to/binary

classes.name: SqlSinkScanner
classes.doc:
Detect raw SQL injection candidates in x86-64 ELF binaries.

Covers MySQL C API (mysql_query, mysql_real_query) and SQLite3
(sqlite3_exec, sqlite3_prepare_v2, sqlite3_prepare).

Algorithm:
  1. Find all SQL sink call sites via PLT resolution.
  2. For each call site, disassemble the enclosing function and walk
     backward from the call to trace the SQL string argument register.
  3. Classify based on provenance:
     - RODATA literal → RODATA_CONST (check for %s → INJECTABLE_LITERAL)
     - snprintf-built stack buffer → inspect format string for %s →
       INJECTABLE or SAFE_NUMERIC
     - Entry register → ARG_PROPAGATED
     - Unresolved → UNKNOWN

sscanf_sink_classifier.py: classify sscanf/scanf/fscanf/vsscanf call sites for
destination buffer overflow via unbounded %s format specifiers.

The question at every input-parsing sink is:
  "Does the format string contain unbounded %s — no explicit width specifier?"

Five verdicts:
  RODATA_SAFE    — format in .rodata, no unbounded %s. ELIMINATED.
  RODATA_UNSAFE  — format in .rodata, has unbounded %s (e.g., "%s %d"). HIGH risk.
  DYNAMIC_FMT    — format built at runtime via snprintf. Cannot verify statically.
                   The libwmshared.so tmplogin parser pattern:
                     snprintf(buf, 32, "%%%zus %%lu %%d", 46) → "%46s %lu %d"
                   would emit DYNAMIC_FMT, reducing manual trace work to:
                   confirm snprintf format template is constant (RODATA).
  ARG_PROPAGATED — format string came from a caller argument. Format injection risk.
  UNKNOWN        — provenance not resolved within look-back window.

Gap this fills vs. SinkArgClassifier:
  SinkArgClassifier covers exec-class sinks (system/popen/execve) and
  snprintf-built buffers passed to those sinks. It does NOT analyze sscanf-family
  format strings for unbounded %s — the class of bug where sscanf(input, "%s", buf)
  overflows buf when input is attacker-controlled.

  Four sscanf callers in libwmshared.so (session 18) required manual disassembly.
  This module would have auto-classified all four and surfaced only the UNKNOWN
  sites for manual follow-up.

Known limitation: %[...] character-class specifiers without a width limit are NOT
  flagged by this module. Only %s without a width specifier is detected as UNSAFE.

Usage:
    from ablation.analyzers.sscanf_sink_classifier import SscanfSinkClassifier

    clf = SscanfSinkClassifier.from_path('/path/to/binary')
    results = clf.classify_all()
    flagged = [r for r in results if r.needs_investigation]
    print(clf.report(results))

    # With existing BinaryContext (avoids redundant LIEF parse):
    from ablation.analyzers.binary_context import BinaryContext
    ctx = BinaryContext.load_or_build(path)
    clf = SscanfSinkClassifier.from_context(ctx)

CLI:
    python3 -m ablation.analyzers.sscanf_sink_classifier /path/to/binary
    python3 -m ablation.analyzers.sscanf_sink_classifier /path/to/binary --flagged-only

classes.name: SscanfSinkClassifier
classes.doc:
Classify sscanf/scanf/fscanf call sites for unbounded %s format specifiers.

Algorithm:
  1. Locate sscanf-family PLT stubs with at least one caller.
  2. For each call site, trace the format argument register backwards.
  3. LEA [rip+x] → .rodata: read string bytes, scan for unbounded %s.
     → RODATA_SAFE or RODATA_UNSAFE.
  4. LEA/MOV → stack slot: search backwards for snprintf that filled it.
     → DYNAMIC_FMT (format was runtime-constructed; verify template manually).
  5. MOV from entry-argument register → ARG_PROPAGATED.
  6. Otherwise → UNKNOWN.

Handles:
  %s         → unbounded (True)
  %20s       → bounded (False)
  %05s       → bounded; '0' is a printf flag, '5' is the width (False)

module_doc:
StageCommitment — No-Lock/Approving audit chain for multi-session RE pipelines.

Three gaps this closes:

1. FORGE is a point-in-time gate; it does not persist a hash of what passed.
   When a finding is revised after confirmation there is no record of the original
   committed content or which session produced it.

2. Multi-session review has no tamper-evidence.  If two agents work on the same
   target across sessions there is no way to detect whether findings were altered
   between sessions without reading both SESSION.md files and diffing by hand.

3. The connection between a confirmed finding and its originating workflow stage
   is not machine-checkable.  FindingRegistry stores findings; it does not record
   how they were produced or who approved them.

Pattern (derived from IBM XFDL No-Lock/Approving signatures):

- Producer calls ``commit()`` with ``lock_mode="no-lock"``.  The content hash is
  recorded but the instance is not frozen — the reviewer may revise it.
- Reviewer calls ``approve()``, optionally passing a ``revised_instance``.  The
  approving hash covers the original ``content_hash`` plus the hash of the revised
  (or original) content, binding both the original commitment and the final result.
- ``verify()`` checks whether the current instance matches the committed or
  approved-revision hash.  Any other value is a tampered state.

Usage::

    sc = StageCommitment(doc_id="cisco/fmc_server")

    # producer commits without locking content
    rec = sc.commit("finding_confirmation", instance, producer="session-42")

    # reviewer approves with optional revision
    rec2 = sc.approve("finding_confirmation", approver="session-43",
                       revised_instance=None)  # None = accept unchanged

    # verify at any later point
    ok, reason = sc.verify("finding_confirmation", instance)
    assert ok

    # human-readable chain report
    print(sc.audit_trail())

    # persist across sessions
    Path("commitments.json").write_text(sc.to_json())
    sc2 = StageCommitment.from_json(Path("commitments.json").read_text())

module_doc:
ELF32 stripped static binary function start discovery via i386 prologue pattern scan.

Motivation: lief populates func_starts only from .symtab / .dynsym entries.
Statically linked stripped i386 ELF binaries have neither table populated.
Without func_starts, SemanticSearcher and TaintTracker cannot run.

Solution: scan every PT_LOAD+PF_X segment for i386 function prologue byte patterns,
with a call-target fallback for binaries compiled with -fomit-frame-pointer (FPO).

    Primary:        55 89 e5      push ebp; mov ebp, esp    (CDECL, ~95% of GCC functions)
    Secondary:      55 57 56      push ebp; push edi; push esi  (callee-save variant)
                    55 53         push ebp; push ebx            (small function variant)
    FPO fallback:   E8 XX XX XX XX  call rel32 target collection
                    Activates when primary+secondary find < 10 starts.
                    All CALL rel32 targets within the exec segment are function entries.
                    GCC -fomit-frame-pointer omits push ebp entirely; call-targets are the
                    only reliable recovery method for these binaries.

False-positive rate for GCC i386 code: low. The 3-byte primary pattern is highly
discriminating — ModRM 0xe5 encodes (mod=11, reg=4/ESP, rm=5/EBP), a combination
that appears inside other instructions only coincidentally.

The FPO fallback has a higher false-positive rate (indirect call targets may be
decoded as direct calls), but is far better than zero functions for large FPO binaries.

Usage:

    from ablation.analyzers.static_elf32_func_start_scanner import StaticELF32FuncStartScanner

    scanner = StaticELF32FuncStartScanner.from_path('/path/to/stripped.elf')
    starts = scanner.scan()                 # List[int] of VAs
    scanner.inject(ctx)                     # push into an existing BinaryContext

Integration note:
    BinaryContext._extract_func_starts() calls this scanner automatically for
    x86_32 binaries when starts < 50 (no eh_frame, no exports, or FPO binary).

module_doc:
static_link_sink_scanner.py: locate exec-class sinks in statically linked ELFs.

Why this exists:
  SinkArgClassifier finds sinks via the PLT. Statically linked binaries (BTT52iFix,
  VE/UninstallAssistantLinux, HMC-V11/img2a, many IBM POWER tools) have no PLT — the
  libc functions are compiled in. SAC returns 0 not because the binary is safe, but
  because there are no PLT stubs to search.

  This module locates the statically-linked implementations of system(), popen(),
  strcpy(), and related sinks using reliable binary signatures, then finds all call
  sites to those implementations, then classifies each call site's argument provenance.

  Gap IDs: SAC-STATIC-001 (system()), SAC-STATIC-002 (popen()), SAC-STATIC-003 (strcpy/strcat).

Strategy:
  system() / popen():
    glibc's system() always contains the string "/bin/sh" as a literal argument to
    execve(). Locate "/bin/sh" in .rodata, find every function that xrefs it with
    a LEA/MOV instruction. The function that also contains a CALL to execve() (or
    that itself loops over a waitpid pattern) is system(). All call sites to that
    function are system() call sites.

  strcpy() / strcat():
    glibc 2.14+ uses SSE2/AVX2 for x86_64 strcpy, making byte-pattern matching
    fragile. Instead, locate C-string sink candidates by scanning for functions whose
    first argument is arg0=rdi and which call memcpy or rep movsb (strcpy). This is
    heuristic and marked UNKNOWN-STATIC. Use BinaryContext str_xrefs to add context.

  Architecture support:
    x86_64: full (system via /bin/sh xref + CALL rel32 scan)
    x86_32: full (system via /bin/sh xref + CALL rel32 i386)
    ppc64 / ppc32 / s390x: /bin/sh xref locates system_impl VA; call scan uses
                            bl/bla instruction encoding.
    Others: /bin/sh xref only; call scan falls back to UNKNOWN-STATIC.

Usage:
    from ablation.analyzers.binary_context import BinaryContext
    from ablation.analyzers.static_link_sink_scanner import StaticLinkSinkScanner

    ctx = BinaryContext.load_or_build('/path/to/static_binary')
    scanner = StaticLinkSinkScanner.from_context(ctx)
    results = scanner.scan_system()
    for r in results:
        print(r)

    print(scanner.report(results))

Scan for PPC64/PPC32 BL (branch and link) instructions targeting `target_va`.
PPC BL encoding: bits[31:26]=0b010010, bits[25:2]=LI (signed 24-bit word offset),
bit[1]=AA (0=relative), bit[0]=LK (1=link).
So instruction = 0x48000001 | (offset & 0x03FFFFFC) where offset is signed
and word-aligned.

Returns (verdict, evidence).

module_doc:
Structured control-flow reconstruction for compiled MCU/ECU firmware.

Converts a basic-block CFG into a tree of structured nodes (Sequence, If,
While) using dominator-tree and natural-loop information.  The output is
equivalent to the source-level control flow of the original C code, without
the goto statements a naive lifter produces.

Algorithm
---------
All compiled automotive firmware (AUTOSAR classic, plain-C ECU code) produces
*reducible* CFGs — every back edge has a unique dominating header.  This lets
us use a dominator-driven Relooper variant that is simpler than the full
Emscripten Relooper:

    1. Walk blocks in RPO (dominators before dominated nodes).
    2. If a block is a loop header (LoopInfo.is_loop_header), emit a WhileNode
       that covers all blocks in the natural loop body, then recurse on the
       blocks beyond the loop exit.
    3. If a block has two successors, look for their closest common post-
       dominator ("join" block).  Emit an IfNode with then/else sub-trees up
       to the join, then continue from the join block.
    4. Otherwise, append the block to the current Sequence and continue.

ISA independence
----------------
The structurizer works on any CFG that exposes:
    - cfg.blocks : Dict[int, Block]   (Block has .start, .succs, .preds, .insns)
    - cfg.entry  : int
    - cfg.flow   : List[(src, dst)]   (forward edges)
    - cfg.flow_r(): List[(dst, src)]  (backward edges — for post-dom)

This matches both `cfg_sh2a.CFG` and `dataflow_engine.CFG`.

Usage::

    from ablation.analyzers.ecu_sh2a_decoder import EcuSH2aDecoder
    from ablation.analyzers.cfg_sh2a import build_cfg
    from ablation.analyzers.structurizer import Structurizer

    dec  = EcuSH2aDecoder(rom, base_va=0)
    insns = dec.disassemble(0, len(rom))
    cfg  = build_cfg(insns)
    s    = Structurizer(cfg)
    tree = s.structure()

    def emitter(insn):
        return f"  // {insn.mnemonic}"

    print(s.emit(emitter))

module_doc:
subsequence_searcher.py: Behavioral subsequence pattern search.

Finds all functions in a binary that contain a specified behavioral
sub-pattern. Two modes:

1. Exact: "find all functions containing [COMPARISON_OP, CONDITIONAL_OP,
   DATA_TRANSFER_OP, UNCONDITIONAL_OP] in sequence": literal subsequence
   match with optional wildcards.

2. DTW approximate: sliding window DTW to find approximate matches,
   warp-invariant (handles small insertions within the pattern).

3. "Like this function": use an existing function's sequence as the pattern
   and find all similar functions in the binary.

Primary RE use cases:
- "Find all handlers that look like the exec handler" (search_like)
- "Find all functions with a cmp+jmp+syscall pattern" (search)
- "Find all functions containing a Tcl_Eval call followed by no error check" (search)

Usage:
    ss = SubsequenceSearcher.from_path('/path/to/binary', ctx=ctx)

    # Exact pattern with wildcards (None = any category):
    pattern = [CAT_INDEX['COMPARISON_OP'], CAT_INDEX['CONDITIONAL_OP'],
               None, CAT_INDEX['UNCONDITIONAL_OP']]
    results = ss.search(pattern)

    # Pattern from category names (more readable):
    pattern = ss.pattern('COMPARISON_OP CONDITIONAL_OP * UNCONDITIONAL_OP')
    results = ss.search(pattern)

    # DTW approximate sliding window:
    results = ss.search_dtw(ref_seq, threshold=0.6)

    # Find functions similar to an existing function:
    results = ss.search_like(ref_va=0x1000, end_va=0x1200, top_k=10)

classes.name: SubsequenceSearcher

Behavioral subsequence pattern search over a binary's functions.

Answers: "which functions in this binary contain this behavioral pattern?"

Three search modes:
1. Exact: literal category sequence with optional wildcards
2. DTW: sliding window approximate match (warp-invariant)
3. Like: find functions similar to an existing function

Uses sliding window DTW: for each function, slides a window of

threshold: minimum similarity score (0..1) to report a match.

mode: 'dtw' (default) or 'sax' (faster pre-filter).

Example: find all handlers that look like the stress exec handler.
    ss.search_like(ref_va=0x1000, end_va=0x1200, top_k=10)

syscall_loongarch64.py: LoongArch64 Linux syscall ABI classification.

ABI (lp64, Linux asm-generic unistd.h):
  $a7: syscall number  (loaded before syscall instruction)
  $a0–$a5: arguments   (up to 6)
  $a0: return value    (negative = -errno)

Syscall numbers match the asm-generic/unistd.h table used by all
LoongArch Linux builds (kernel 5.x+). LoongArch does NOT have a
custom syscall table — it uses the generic ABI directly.

Source: linux/arch/loongarch/include/uapi/asm/unistd.h
        linux/include/uapi/asm-generic/unistd.h (6.6 kernel)

  "escalation" — privilege escalation
Returns None if unknown or unclassified.

module_doc:
Forward taint tracker for x86-64 stripped ELF binaries.

Usage:
    from ablation.analyzers.taint_tracker import TaintTracker
    tt = TaintTracker('/path/to/binary')
    sinks = tt.trace_function(
        func_va=0x22ccc0,
        tainted_args=['rdi', 'rsi', 'rdx'],
        max_insns=500
    )
    for sink in sinks:
        print(sink)

Returns a list of TaintSink objects describing where tainted data reaches:
    - alloc_size: tainted value used as allocation size argument
    - copy_len: tainted value used as copy/move length
    - mem_write: tainted value written to memory
    - branch_cond: tainted value controls a branch (determines reachability)
    - call_arg: tainted value passed to a function call

Limitations:
    - Intra-function only (does not follow calls)
    - No path sensitivity (conservative: union of all paths)
    - No loop unrolling (assumes loops can execute any number of times)
    - Handles: mov, movzx, movsxd, lea (partial), add, sub, imul, shl, shr, and, or, xor
    - Tracks general-purpose 64-bit registers + stack slots (rsp+offset, rbp-offset)

methods.name: trace_function
methods.doc:
Trace taint forward through function starting at func_va.
tainted_args: list of register names that are tainted at function entry,
              e.g. ['rdi', 'rsi', 'rdx']
Returns list of TaintSink where taint reaches interesting operations.

module_doc:
taint_tracker_arc.py: Synopsys DesignWare ARC network-to-sink taint analysis.

Architecture: ARC 700 / ARC HS (ARC EM, HS3x, HS4x, HS5x).
ABI: ARC Linux ABI (GNU toolchain convention):
     r0-r7  argument registers (8 integer args), r0 return value.
     r0-r12 caller-saved (volatile). r13-r25 callee-saved.
     r26 = GP (global pointer), r27 = FP, r28 = SP, r31 = BLINK (LR).
     No branch delay slots.

Prologue: push_s blink        [save return address, compact 16-bit]
          push_s fp           [save frame pointer]
          sub sp, sp, N       [allocate stack frame]
Return:   j_s [blink]         [compact 16-bit return]
          OR j [blink]        [32-bit return]
Call:     bl <target>         [direct call, 25-bit offset]
          jl [reg]            [indirect call via register]

Note: capstone 5.x has no CS_ARCH_ARC. This tracker uses a pure-Python ARC
instruction walker (arc_decoder.ARCDecoder) for control-flow classification
and lief/pyelftools for PLT/symbol extraction. Full instruction-level decode
will be available when capstone 6.x adds ARC support.

Sources: recv/recvfrom/read/fgets/gets/fread -- return value in r0.
Sinks  : system/execve/execl/execvp/popen/strcpy/sprintf/memcpy/strcat/snprintf.

Targets: Synopsys DesignWare ARC EM (IoT/MCU), ARC HS38/HS48 (SMP Linux),
         ARC 770D (multimedia/storage), smart TV SoCs (Marvell, Sigma Designs),
         automotive SoCs, Seagate/Western Digital storage controllers.

Usage:
    from ablation.analyzers.taint_tracker_arc import ARCTaintTracker
    tracker = ARCTaintTracker.from_path('arc_binary')
    findings = tracker.run()
    chains   = tracker.run_interprocedural(depth=4)

taint_tracker_arm32.py: Static intraprocedural ARM32/Thumb taint analysis.

Finds data-flow paths from network receive taint sources to dangerous sinks.
Implements the libdft taint policy adapted for ARM32 AAPCS:

  XFER  (mov/ldr):           dst_taint = src_taint
  ALU   (add/sub/and/orr/eor/mul): dst_taint |= operand taints
  CLR   (mov rd, #0; eor rd, rd): dst_taint = {}
  LOAD  (ldr rd, [rn, #off]): dst_taint = stack_slot_taint(rn+off)
  STORE (str rs, [rn, #off]): stack_slot_taint(rn+off) = src_taint
  CALL  (source):            r0 tainted; buffer args tracked
  CALL  (sink):              alert if relevant arg register tainted
  CALL  (other):             r0-r3, r12 cleared (AAPCS caller-saved)

Stack model: tracks [sp + N] and [sp - N] slots using sp-relative offsets.
Writeback addressing (STR rd, [sp, #-N]! and LDM/STM push/pop) updates the
sp delta tracker.

Usage:
    from ablation.analyzers.taint_tracker_arm32 import ARM32TaintTracker, TaintFinding32

    tracker = ARM32TaintTracker('/path/to/libhijoyptt.so')
    findings = tracker.run_on_function(func_va=0x2511c)
    for f in findings:
        print(f)

    # Interprocedural mode (all functions in binary):
    findings = tracker.run_interprocedural()

module_doc:
Forward labeled-taint tracker for 32-bit ARM (A32) and Thumb-2 (T32) instruction streams.

State
-----
* ``regs``       register family -> Taint. Core registers are whole 32-bit values.
                 VFP s/d registers are lanes of their q family (ARM ARM A2.6.2):
                 a write to s3 merges into q0.
* ``mem``        (region, offset) -> Taint. Stack frame is region named ``sp``.
* ``ranges``     byte ranges of a region that are tainted (syscall input buffers).
* ``mem_ptrs``   slot -> pointer fact it holds (spilled pointer registers).
* ``eq``         register equality classes (full-width copies).
* ``ra_regs``    register families that currently hold the return address.
* ``ra_slots``   frame slots that hold the return address.

Conditional execution (``addeq``, IT blocks) is path-insensitive: the state
after is the join of with-and-without the instruction.

This tracker consumes instruction streams (from_listing / from_objdump /
from_capstone). For binary RE over ELF files use taint_tracker_arm32.py.

Usage:
    from ablation.analyzers.taint_tracker_arm32_labeled import TaintTracker, Mode, Policy
    from ablation.analyzers.insn_arm32 import from_listing

    t = TaintTracker(Mode.THUMB)
    t.taint_memory("r0", 0, "buf", 4096)
    findings = t.run(list(from_listing(text, Mode.THUMB)))
    for f in findings:
        print(f)

module_doc:
taint_tracker_arm64.py: AArch64 data-flow taint tracker.

Labeled-taint model: Taint(labels, bound).
Key AArch64 semantics:
  - Every W-register write zero-extends: result is bounded to 0xFFFFFFFF.
  - ``and rd, rn, #imm``: bitmask with top bit set = alignment mask = no bound;
    positive mask = bounds rd.
  - Shift/extend modifiers on source operands scale the bound.
  - ldp/stp pair instructions; pre/post-index writeback.
  - Linux arm64 syscall: x8=nr, x0-x5=args, x0=result; read/recvfrom taints buffer.

Sources: recv/read/readv and Linux svc (read/recvfrom syscalls)
Sinks:   system/execve/strcpy/sprintf/memcpy and other dangerous libc functions

AAPCS64: x0-x7 args, x0-x1 return, x19-x28 callee-saved, x30=lr, x29=fp.

Like from_path but augments symbols with:

    internal functions are scanned, not just exports.

methods.name: from_path_ko
methods.doc:
Kernel module variant (.ko).

Kernel modules are relocatable objects — BL instructions targeting external
symbols have displacement=0 before the kernel loader patches them.  The
.rela.text section contains R_AARCH64_CALL26/JUMP26 entries that map
instruction offsets to their real external symbol names.  This method injects
those entries into _syms so the taint engine resolves them transparently.

module_doc:
Forward taint tracker for x86-32 (i386) stripped ELF binaries.

Addresses the gap in TaintTracker (x86-64 only): i386 cdecl passes all
arguments on the stack ([ebp+8]=arg1, [ebp+c]=arg2, ...).  The initial
taint source is a set of EBP-relative offsets (e.g. {0x2c} = arg10),
not a set of register names.

Usage:
    from ablation.analyzers.taint_tracker_i386 import TaintTrackerI386
    tt = TaintTrackerI386('/path/to/i386.elf')
    sinks = tt.trace_function(
        func_va=0x839c14f,
        tainted_ebp_offsets={0x2c},   # [ebp+0x2c] = arg10 tainted at entry
        max_insns=2000,
    )
    for sink in sinks: print(sink)

Why this exists:
    TaintTracker uses CS_MODE_64 and SysV x86-64 register ARG_REGS.
    i386 cdecl has no register-passed args; all arguments are EBP-relative
    stack slots.  Tracking whether a specific stack argument flows to a call
    sink requires a different initial-taint model and a push-tracking model.

Limitation vs x86-64 tracker:
    - No inter-procedural analysis (stays within the traced function)
    - Conservative (union across all paths, no path sensitivity)
    - Handles push/pop taint propagation for i386 call convention

classes.name: TaintTrackerI386
classes.doc:
Forward taint tracker for i386 stripped ELF binaries.

Taint sources are EBP-relative stack offsets (function arguments in
cdecl calling convention) specified as a set of positive integers.
Example: {0x2c} taints [ebp+0x2c] = arg10.

methods.name: trace_function
methods.doc:
Trace tainted EBP-relative stack slots forward through the function.

tainted_ebp_offsets: set of positive offsets from EBP that are
    tainted at function entry.  E.g. {0x2c} = arg10 in a cdecl
    function where arg1=[ebp+8].

Returns list of TaintSink32 where tainted data reaches a sink.

functions.name: _elf_load_base
functions.doc:
Return the lowest PT_LOAD p_vaddr for a 32-bit ELF, or 0 for PIE/unknown.
Used to convert VA → file offset: file_off = va - load_base + p_offset.
For common non-PIE i386 binaries (base=0x8048000, p_offset=0), this
gives file_off = va - 0x8048000.  For PIE (base=0), file_off = va.

functions.name: _regs_in
functions.doc: Return canonical register names that appear in a memory expression.

functions.name: _extract_ebp_offset
functions.doc:
Parse an EBP-relative memory expression and return the signed offset.
Examples:
    'ebp + 0x2c'  → 0x2c
    'ebp - 0x8'   → -0x8 (not positive, so ignored for arg tracking)
    'ebp'         → 0
Returns None if parsing fails.

module_doc:
taint_tracker_loongarch64.py: LoongArch64 data-flow taint tracker.

Labeled-taint model: Taint(labels: frozenset, bound: Optional[int]).
andi zeros the upper bits of the result and can bound the taint range.
addi.d on $sp is tracked as a frame-offset rebase.

ABI (lp64):
  $a0–$a7:  argument registers (8 regs)
  $a0–$a1:  return values
  $t0–$t8:  caller-saved temporaries
  $ra:      return address (caller-saved; written by bl/jirl)
  $fp/$s0–$s8: callee-saved

Sources: recv/recvfrom/recvmsg/read/fgets/gets/fread (return value in $a0)
Sinks:   system/execve/execl/execvp/execle/execvpe/popen/
         strcpy/strcat/sprintf/vsprintf/snprintf/vsnprintf/memcpy/memmove/gets

Targets: TencentOS 4.6 LoongArch64 binaries — glibc, OpenSSL, QEMU,
         kernel modules, EDK2, GRUB2 EFI, cryptography libraries.
         Corpus: /media/cowboy/research/TencentOS/

Like from_path but augments function boundaries from three sources:

  1. .eh_frame FDE initial_location (present in stripped binaries)
  2. .debug_info DW_TAG_subprogram low_pc / high_pc (requires -g)
  3. .BTF.ext func_info (kernel modules)

addi.d prologue heuristic misses leaf or tail-call-optimised functions.

methods.name: from_system_map
methods.doc:
Like from_path but loads symbol names from a kernel System.map file.
Use for vmlinux analysis where the binary is stripped but System.map
provides the canonical VA->name mapping (62k+ functions on TencentOS 6.6.119).

System.map format per line: <hex_va> <type> <name>
Only T/t/W/w (text function / weak) entries are injected; data symbols
(D/d/R/r/B/b/A/a) are excluded since the tracker only resolves call targets.
System.map entries take precedence over stripped ELF symtab entries.

Usage:

        '/path/to/vmlinux', '/boot/System.map-6.6.119')
    findings = tt.run_interprocedural()

Seeded intraprocedural scan for library RE: treats the specified
argument registers as tainted at function entry, then tracks to sinks.

Useful for shared library analysis where external input arrives through
function arguments rather than through recv/read call sites.

Args:

    seed_arg_indices: Which argument registers to seed (0-7 → $a0-$a7).
                      Defaults to [0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7] (all args tainted).
    source_label:     Taint label applied to seeded registers.

Interprocedural BFS: follow tainted $a0-$a7 from callers into callees.

Each callee that receives tainted argument registers is re-scanned with
those labels as its initial state. Recursion depth bounded by `depth`.

Handle a 'syscall 0' frame in the taint scan.

Reads $a7 from the constant-folding table to identify the syscall number.
Source syscalls taint $a0 with the syscall label.
Sink/escalation syscalls emit a finding if any of $a0–$a5 are tainted.
Unknown $a7: conservatively clobber caller-saved and continue.

imported function name without the ±_PLT_TOL scan.

taint_tracker_mips.py: MIPS32 network-to-sink taint analysis.

taint_tracker_mips64.py: MIPS64 network-to-sink taint analysis.

Architecture: MIPS64 big-endian and little-endian.

consumes the delay-slot instruction before processing the branch outcome.

arithmetic; DMULT/DMULTU/DDIV/DDIVU for wide multiply/divide; DSLL/DSRL/DSRA
and their 32-suffix variants for doubleword shifts.

         Return value in $v0; taint propagates from there.
Sinks  : system/execve/execl/execvp/popen/strcpy/sprintf/memcpy/strcat/snprintf.

    tracker = MIPS64TaintTracker.from_path('iosd', endian='big')
    findings = tracker.run()

module_doc:
Forward labeled-taint tracker for MIPS32 (o32) and MIPS64 (n64) instruction streams.

State
-----
* ``regs``      canonical register -> Taint. GPRs are whole values; ``hi``/``lo``
                and ``fcc`` are tracked like registers.
* ``mem``       (region, offset) -> Taint. The stack frame is region ``$29`` (sp).
* ``ranges``, ``mem_ptrs``, ``eq``, ``ra_regs``/``ra_slots`` as in armtaint.

MIPS specifics
--------------
* **Branch delay slots.** ``jal``/``jalr``/``jr``/``b*`` (non-Release-6) execute
  the following instruction before transferring control. The tracker defers the
  transfer's effect until after its slot; a branch-likely slot is joined
  path-insensitively.
* **MIPS64 narrowing.** 32-bit-result ops (``addu``, ``sll``, ``lw``, etc.)
  sign-extend from bit 31. A bound survives only if it is below 2**31; pointer
  facts never survive narrowing.
* **Returns.** ``jr $ra`` (and ``jr`` of any register in ra_regs). The saved-ra
  slot is whatever ``sw/sd $ra`` wrote.

Feed instruction streams from ``from_listing`` / ``from_objdump`` / ``from_capstone``
in ``insn_mips``. For binary RE over ELF files use taint_tracker_mips.py.

Usage:
    from ablation.analyzers.taint_tracker_mips_labeled import TaintTracker, Mode, Policy
    from ablation.analyzers.insn_mips import from_listing

    t = TaintTracker(Mode.MIPS32)
    t.taint_memory("$a0", 0, "buf", 4096)
    findings = t.run(list(from_listing(text, Mode.MIPS32)))

methods.doc: Conservative join (union). ``widen=True`` collapses differing bounds to None.

module_doc:
taint_tracker_nanomips.py: nanoMIPS network-to-sink taint analysis.

Architecture: nanoMIPS (variable-width 16/32/48-bit instructions).
              Ingenic X-series SoCs (JZ4780, X1000, X2000), MediaTek Helio
              embedded, MIPS32r6 microcontrollers.

ABI: O32-compatible (same register assignments as MIPS32):
     $a0-$a3 args, $v0/$v1 return, $t0-$t9 caller-saved, $s0-$s7 callee-saved.

Key ISA differences from MIPS32:
  - No branch delay slots (removed in nanoMIPS).
  - Calls: BALC (P16 and P32 forms), JALRC (P32) — replaces JAL/JALR.
  - Returns: JRC $ra — replaces JR $ra.
  - Variable-width instructions: 16, 32, or 48 bytes.
  - P32 BALC: bits[31:26] = 0x2a, bits[25:0] = signed offset; target = VA + 4 + sign_extend_26(offset) << 1.
  - P16 BALC: bits[15:10] = 0b110010, bits[9:0] = signed offset; target = VA + 2 + sign_extend_10(offset) << 1.

Two execution paths:
  1. Full decode (capstone 6.x with CS_MODE_NANOMIPS): uses capstone operand detail;
     register-level taint propagation identical to MIPS32 tracker.
  2. Fallback (capstone 5.x or no capstone): NanoMIPSDecoder frame-walk;
     BALC target extracted by bit-field decode; conservative taint (all $a0-$a3
     marked tainted after any source call — no false negatives, possible false positives).

Sources: recv, recvfrom, read, fgets, gets, fread, recvmsg and PLT wrappers.
Sinks:   system, popen, execve, execl, execvp, strcpy, strcat, sprintf, snprintf,
         fprintf, memcpy, memmove, bcopy, write, send, sendto.

Usage:
    from ablation.analyzers.taint_tracker_nanomips import NanoMIPSTaintTracker

    tracker = NanoMIPSTaintTracker.from_path('firmware.elf')
    findings = tracker.run()
    chains   = tracker.run_interprocedural(depth=4)
    print(tracker.report(findings))

nanoMIPS taint tracker. Supports intraprocedural and interprocedural modes.

Automatically selects full decode (capstone 6.x) or conservative fallback.

    findings = tracker.run()
    chains   = tracker.run_interprocedural(depth=4)
    print(tracker.report(findings))

Register-level propagation is unavailable without full decode, so we use

This produces no false negatives at the cost of possible false positives.

taint_tracker_ppc32.py: PowerPC 32-bit network-to-sink taint analysis.

Architecture: PPC32 big-endian and little-endian (POWER LE Linux).
ABI: System V / EABI: r3-r10 args (8 integer regs), r3 return value,
     r13-r31 callee-saved, r0/r3-r12/lr caller-saved. No branch delay slots.

Prologue: stwu r1, -N(r1)  [allocate frame + save old SP]
          mflr r0           [save link register]
Return:   blr               [branch to link register]
Call:     bl  <target>      [direct call]
          bctrl             [indirect call via CTR, used for PLT]

Sources: recv/recvfrom/read/fgets/gets/fread -- return value in r3.
Sinks  : system/execve/execl/execvp/popen/strcpy/sprintf/memcpy/strcat/snprintf.

Targets: Cisco 7200/3700 series IOS (big-endian), MikroTik RB600 (big-endian),
         VxWorks embedded (big-endian), POWER LE Linux userspace (little-endian),
         older Fortinet hardware (big-endian).

Usage:
    from ablation.analyzers.taint_tracker_ppc32 import PPC32TaintTracker
    tracker = PPC32TaintTracker.from_path('iosd')          # big-endian default
    findings = tracker.run()
    chains   = tracker.run_interprocedural(depth=4)

classes.doc:
Source-to-sink static taint tracker for PPC32 ELF binaries.

ABI: System V / EABI. No branch delay slots.

Usage:

    findings = tracker.run()
    chains   = tracker.run_interprocedural(depth=4)

Custom sinks:
    tracker = PPC32TaintTracker.from_path('fw', custom_sinks={'vxExecCmd': [0]})

From BinaryContext:
